attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hard-coded white (#ffffff) on a background of var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the default light theme. The label is invisible in the default theme, so the feature's purpose is not delivered and it fails WCAG 1.4.3.

The unpublish control is a clickable span with only onClick: no button role, tabIndex, or key handler. Keyboard-only editors cannot reach or activate it, failing WCAG 2.1.1 for a user group the context names explicitly.

The unpublish control has no accessible name. Its only child is an aria-hidden icon, and there is no aria-label or hidden text, so screen readers announce nothing meaningful (WCAG 4.1.2). A trash icon also suggests deletion although the action returns the story to drafts.
attacks.evidence: <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" /> inside <span className={styles.unpublish} onClick={handleUnpublish}> with no aria-label

attacks.claim: The unpublish affordance has a hover style but no :focus-visible style, so focus would be invisible even once the control becomes focusable (WCAG 2.4.7).
attacks.evidence: .unpublish:hover { color: var(--danger); background: var(--surface-hover); } (no focus-visible rule)

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish has no error handling and no in-flight guard. A rejected onUnpublish is an unhandled rejection with no user feedback, so the editor may believe a story left the site when it is still live. Repeated clicks during the request can open multiple confirms or send duplicate unpublish requests.

The diff shows only a client-side confirm guarding the destructive unpublish. The server-side authorization of onUnpublish is outside this diff, so it cannot be verified here. It is likely enforced by the existing API and is not a defect of this change.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: server-side authorization for the unpublish call is not in the diff

attacks.claim: The embargo flag is computed once per render from new Date(), so the badge stays after the lift time passes until some other re-render. It also relies on the browser clock.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();

attacks.claim: After a successful unpublish, the row's status comes from the prop and the diff shows no refetch or update. The row may keep showing published with the unpublish icon, depending on the parent's wiring.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any state update or refetch after onUnpublish(draft.id)

attacks.claim: The embargo lift time is shown with no timezone label or year, so editors in other zones or across a year boundary may misread it.
The PR adds time-dependent embargo logic and a confirm-then-unpublish flow with no tests, and the embargo predicate is inline with a non-null assertion.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no test changes for DraftRow, the embargo predicate, or handleUnpublish
